I'll start by reading the docs and looking at the workspace.

The last call was cut off before it ran. I'll write the script with `write_file`.

I wrote `/app/bin/hourly.py` and ran it on `/app/data`. The result is in `/app/out/hourly.json`, and `/app/STATUS.json` says `success`.

- **Checker:** `python tools/check_hourly.py` reports every hourly value matching the approved values: 1131 of 1131 hours for each of the six quantities.
- **Unit tests:** `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` ran 4 tests, all OK.

The script follows the documented rules rather than anything specific to the current files. Conversions and range checks use exact fractions, so a value on a range bound, such as 333.15 K, is not pushed out by float error. It uses only the standard library, and I changed nothing under `/app/data`, `/app/docs`, `/app/tests` or `/app/tools`.

The docs don't say what to do with a `units` line that names a unit the rules don't list. I treat the values of that quantity as missing.

I wrote /app/bin/hourly.py and ran it on /app/data. The result is in /app/out/hourly.json, and /app/STATUS.json says success.

- Checker: python tools/check_hourly.py reports every hourly value matching the approved values: 1131 of 1131 hours for each of the six quantities.
- Unit tests: python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . ran 4 tests, all OK.

The script follows the documented rules rather than anything specific to the current files. Conversions and range checks use exact fractions, so a value on a range bound, such as 333.15 K, is not pushed out by float error. It uses only the standard library, and I changed nothing under /app/data, /app/docs, /app/tests or /app/tools.

The docs don't say what to do with a units line that names a unit the rules don't list. I treat the values of that quantity as missing.

command_result.command: cd /app; find . -path ./data -prune -o -type f -print | head -100; ls data | head -50; ls data | wc -l; cat docs/overview.md

cd /app; cat tools/check_hourly.py | head -60; sed -n 1,60p tests/test_hourly.py; head -c 600 tools/approved-hourly.json; cd data; head -15 dump-1024b5.log; grep -h '^#' *.log | sed 's/:.*//' | sort | uniq -c; grep -h '^#' *.log | grep -v -E '^# (station|upload|interval|tz|columns|units|sync|firmware):' | sort | uniq -c | head -20; grep -h '^# units' *.log | sort | uniq -c; ls | grep -v '\.log$'; file * | grep -v 'ASCII text$' | head
cd /app; mkdir -p out; python3 bin/hourly.py data out/hourly.json && python tools/check_hourly.py; python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -5

cd /app; python3 - <<'EOF'
p='bin/hourly.py'
s=open(p).read()
a=s.index('                lg = rf = None')
b=s.index('                if lg is not None and rf is not None:')
new='''                ml = re.search(r"logger=\\s*(\\d{4}-\\d\\d-\\d\\d[ T]\\d\\d:\\d\\d:\\d\\d)", val)
                mr = re.search(r"ref=\\s*(\\d{4}-\\d\\d-\\d\\dT\\d\\d:\\d\\d:\\d\\dZ)", val)
                lg = ml.group(1) if ml else None
                rf = mr.group(1) if mr else None
'''
open(p,'w').write(s[:a]+new+s[b:])
EOF
sed -n 112,125p bin/hourly.py; python3 bin/hourly.py data out/hourly.json && python tools/check_hourly.py; python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -15

cd /app; echo '{"status":"success","summary":"Wrote /app/bin/hourly.py following the documented rules (units, tz, sync drift, dedup by upload, coverage, vector wind mean, rain increments) and generated /app/out/hourly.json. The unit tests and tools/check_hourly.py both pass."}' > STATUS.json; python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('STATUS.json')))"
